app.simulatedModeBody: Configs are read from a sample directory, not a real host. Control commands run in simulation, and probe/metric values are synthetic — they exist to demonstrate the interface. To work against a real server, run with NKT_MODE=local.
app.readOnlyMode: Changes are disabled by the NKT_ALLOW_MUTATIONS=false setting — the interface is read-only.

login.subtitle: Network resource map, config auditing, and host service management.
login.adminPasswordNote: The admin password is printed to the server log on first startup.

common.confirmDelete: Delete the {{what}} {{name}}? This can't be undone.
common.mutationsDisabled: Actions unavailable: needs the admin role and mutations enabled.

packageInstall.title: Installing {{packageName}}
packageInstall.connectError: Could not connect to the install session.
packageInstall.failed: Installation failed{{code}}. See the output above for what went wrong.

passwordForm.sessionsEnd: Changing your password ends every session — you'll need to sign in again.
passwordForm.forgot: Forgot your password and can't sign in? On the host, run sudo nkt passwd — this sets a new admin password without touching accumulated history.

updateModal.title: Package update
updateModal.willOffer: About to offer an update for: {{names}}. Confirmation (Y/n) happens right in the window below, like a normal terminal.
updateModal.connectError: Could not connect to the update session.
updateModal.rescanned: Host rescanned — the package list is already up to date.
updateModal.failed: Update failed{{code}}. See the output above for what went wrong.

findings.title: Configuration issues
findings.hint: The result of matching nginx, haproxy, and docker configs against the host's actual listeners and firewall rules. Each entry has an explanation and a concrete action.

audit.title: Audit log
audit.hint: Every change to the host's state — a service restart, a config edit, a firewall rule — is logged with the user, the result, and the command output.

interfaces.noLinkTooltip: Administratively enabled, but no response from the link partner — an unplugged cable, a disabled switch port, or the peer isn't up
interfaces.guessTooltip: Guessed from the interface name — not verified, unlike the docker labels above
interfaces.title: Network interfaces
interfaces.hint: Everything actually on the host per ip addr: physical NICs, bridges, VLANs, tunnels, loopback. Which one is public isn't decided here — that's determined precisely per-socket on the Overview, Firewall, and Findings pages.

users.title: Accounts
users.hint: Who can sign in to the web interface, and with what role. Passwords are stored irreversibly (argon2id) — a forgotten password can only be reset by setting a new one, via sudo nkt passwd <username> on the host itself.
users.confirmDelete: Delete the account {{username}}? This can't be undone.
users.roleHint: viewer is read-only, admin is full host control

lxd.hint: LXD containers and virtual machines — one tool manages both instance types.
lxd.none: LXD not found, or there are no instances.
lxd.newInstanceHint: lxc launch — the image downloads automatically, the instance starts right away.

podman.hint: Containers on Podman, a separate engine from docker — the same operations: start, stop, delete.
podman.none: Podman not found, or there are no containers.
podman.newContainerHint: The image is pulled if needed, the container is created and started right away.

docker.hint: Matching what's declared in compose against what's actually running.

virt.transientTooltip: Transient domain: not registered via virsh define, so it has no saved definition or autostart. Disappears from the list when stopped.
virt.forceDestroyTooltip: Immediate forced shutdown — like pulling the power cord
virt.confirmDeleteWithDisks: Delete the VM {{name}} together with its disks? Disk images will be permanently deleted.
virt.confirmDeleteDefinition: Delete the VM {{name}}'s definition? Disks stay in place.
virt.title: Virtual machines
virt.hint: libvirt/QEMU domains — managed via virsh. Created and edited through the XML definition.
virt.none: libvirt not found, or there are no domains.
virt.newVmHint: Both paths end the same way — reviewing and editing the XML before saving.
virt.createDiskFile: Create the disk file (qemu-img create) — without this the XML will reference a file that doesn't exist
virt.invalidName: The name may only contain Latin letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores
virt.applyVirshDefine: Apply (virsh define) — without this the XML is saved, but the domain isn't registered

hosts.tunnelActiveTooltip: SSH is currently unreachable — the dashboard, terminal, and reinstall/update are running over the fallback channel
hosts.tunnelConnectedTooltip: Fallback channel is connected and ready, but not currently in use — SSH is working
hosts.tunnelDisconnectedTooltip: Fallback channel is enabled in settings, but the hub hasn't connected to the host yet
hosts.notificationDenied: The browser didn't grant notification permission.
hosts.confirmForeignInstall:
This host already has nkt installed, not by this hub: {{detail}}.

Continue anyway? The binary, systemd unit, and env will be overwritten, and the admin password synced to what the hub stores — if this is someone else's install, access with its current password will be lost.
hosts.confirmRemoveSudo:
Remove passwordless sudo from "{{user}}" on "{{name}}"?

The hub won't be able to push updates or change anything on the host that needs root, until access is granted again (or the SSH user becomes root).
hosts.confirmStopHost: Stop nkt on "{{name}}"? The host will become unreachable through the hub until you start it again.
hosts.confirmBulkStart: Start nkt on every host at once ({{count}})?
hosts.confirmBulkStop: Stop nkt on every host at once ({{count}})? They'll all become unreachable through the hub until you start them again.
hosts.confirmImport: Import hosts from this file? Hosts are added alongside existing ones (the file doesn't replace or dedupe by name/address). Secrets in the file only decrypt if it was exported with this same hub's NKT_HUB_MASTER_KEY.
hosts.confirmRemoveHost: Remove the host "{{name}}" from the hub? nkt itself is not removed from it.
hosts.thisMachine: this machine — the hub scans itself, no SSH
hosts.title: Hosts
hosts.hint: Each host is a separate VPS running its own nkt: the hub pushes the binary over SSH, sets it up as a systemd service, and proxies requests to it — so the dashboard and controls look no different from a plain single-host nkt.
hosts.exportWithKeyTooltip: For moving to a new hub without manually copying NKT_HUB_MASTER_KEY — the file becomes self-sufficient to decrypt, so keep it as carefully as passwords
hosts.notifyTooltip: Notifies via the browser about a new critical/high problem, or lost contact with a host — while this tab stays open
hosts.noHosts: No hosts yet — add the first one below.
hosts.jobRunning: in progress — you can close this window, the install continues in the background.
hosts.publicKeyBody: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the host itself (for the user given when it was added), then click "install". The matching private half is stored only on the hub and never leaves it.
hosts.confirmExportUnencrypted:
Download WITHOUT encryption?

The export file is plain JSON carrying the hub's own encryption key plus SSH/admin secrets for every host — whoever has the file has them. Without a password, anyone who gets it reads everything directly.
hosts.exportWithKeyBody: This file carries the hub's own encryption key plus every host's SSH/admin secrets in the clear — anyone who gets it can decrypt everything. Strongly recommended to encrypt it with a password right now rather than keep it as-is. The password isn't stored anywhere — lose it and the file becomes useless.
hosts.encryptPasswordLabel: Password to encrypt the file (optional, but recommended)
hosts.encryptedFileBody: "{{fileName}}" is password-protected — enter it to decrypt and import the hosts.
hosts.secretKeyEditing: New private key (PEM) — leave empty to keep the current one
hosts.secretPasswordEditing: New password — leave empty to keep the current one
hosts.name: Name
hosts.generatedKeyHint: No need to paste a private key anywhere — the hub generates its own pair and shows the public half after saving, which needs to be added to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the host.
hosts.generatedKeyHintReplace: This host's previous auth method will be replaced by the new key.
hosts.terminalEnabled: enable a web terminal on the host
hosts.terminalEnabledHint: A full root shell right in the browser (the "Terminal" section on the host itself) — off by default.
hosts.reinstallsOnChange: Changing this setting immediately reinstalls nkt on the host (if already installed) to apply it.
hosts.appliesOnFirstInstall: Applies on this host's first install.
hosts.tunnelEnabled: fallback channel for when SSH is unreachable
hosts.tunnelEnabledHint: The hub keeps a separate secured connection to the host (port 8078 by default — NKT_HUB_TUNNEL_PORT on the hub) so the dashboard, terminal, and reinstall/update keep working even if SSH stops responding to it. No need to configure the hub's own address — the hub dials in the same way it does over SSH, using the same host address. On by default for new hosts; doesn't replace SSH for the very first install (nothing to fall back to yet).
hosts.addHostHint: The hub will connect over SSH, detect the architecture, build or reuse a cached nkt binary, and install it as a systemd service

certs.title: TLS certificates
certs.hint: Reads the files referenced by nginx's ssl_certificate and haproxy's crt directives. Checks expiry, name coverage, key strength, whether autorenewal will actually fire, and — via a separate TLS connection to the socket — whether the file on disk matches what clients actually see.
certs.scheduleHint: Time to expiry on a shared one-year scale — the order in which certificates will stop working
certs.noCertsDirectives: No ssl_certificate directive found in any parsed config.
certs.thresholdsNote: Thresholds: {{warn}}d — warning, {{critical}}d — urgent. Let's Encrypt renews 30 days before expiry, so a shorter runway means autorenewal already didn't fire.
certs.confirmRenewDerived: This is a copy of the certificate from {{source}} — the original will be renewed, and this copy will be automatically rebuilt from the new certificate and key, then the service reloaded.
certs.jobRunning: In progress — you can close this window, the process continues on the host in the background.
certs.unattachedHint: Present in /etc/letsencrypt/live, but no parsed config references them — everything certbot certonly issued (by hand or via the form above) lands here until something connects it to a service
certs.unattachedFooter: For a certificate to show up in "Details" above — wire it into a service's config (the "Configs" page) or assemble a PEM for haproxy with the form below.
certs.specifyDomain: Enter at least one domain name
certs.confirmIssue:
Issue a certificate for {{domains}}?

certbot certonly --standalone needs port 80/443 free — nginx and haproxy will be briefly stopped and automatically started back up once it finishes.
certs.issueTitle: Issue a new Let's Encrypt certificate
certs.issueHint: For a domain that doesn't have a certificate yet — certbot certonly --standalone. Wildcard names aren't supported: standalone proves ownership of only one exact name at a time.
certs.combineTitle: Assemble a haproxy PEM from certbot
certs.combineHint: Takes an already-issued certbot certificate from /etc/letsencrypt/live and glues it to its key into one file — what haproxy's crt needs. Doesn't call certbot renew.
certs.combinedSnippet: {{lineage}}: PEM assembled, valid until {{date}}. It isn't wired into any service yet — paste the directive below into the right file via the "Configs" page.
certs.combinedFileSuffix: was written, valid until {{date}}. haproxy reloaded its config — nothing to paste.
certs.listUpdated: The certificate list is already up to date.
certs.selfSignedHint: For internal services, or as a stopgap until a trusted-CA certificate is ready — the browser will still show a warning
certs.selfSignedResult: Certificate for {{names}} created, valid until {{date}}. It isn't wired into any service yet — paste the directives below into the right file via the "Configs" page.

fw.confirmCriticalPort:
WARNING: port {{port}} is the standard SSH port.

{{action}} could cut off SSH access to this host. An already-open session usually won't drop right away, but the next connection attempt will fail. Recovering access would then only be possible through the hosting provider's console or physical access.

Continue anyway?
fw.ufwOffNote: ufw is currently off — the rule is saved, but has no effect until you enable it.
fw.selectOneOption: Pick at least one: apply now or save permanently.
fw.confirmQuickAllow: Allow {{port}}/{{protocol}} in ufw from any source?
fw.ufwDisabledNote: ufw is off — has no effect
fw.hint: The full set of iptables, ufw, and firewalld rules with counters. Rules only change through ufw/firewalld: editing iptables directly from the web interface is a sure way to lock yourself out of the server.
fw.notInstalled: {{label}} is not installed on this host.
fw.addFirewalldRuleHint: A port or service in a zone, logged
fw.ufwRulesHint: Numbers shift after every change, so deletion is checked against the exact text you see.
fw.allRulesHint: Counters come from iptables-save -c: a zero counter means the rule has never matched.
fw.socketsHint: ss output: what's actually listening on ports

topology.title: Resource map
topology.hint: Red for critical problems, yellow for warnings. Hover or click a node to see the whole route — from the external network to the backend and back — and its details.
topology.findingsHint: {{count}} findings on the map — click a node for details
topology.clickNodeHint: Click a node on the map for details.

configs.confirmRollback: Restore version #{{id}}? The file's current content will be replaced.
configs.title: Configs
configs.hint: Files found while parsing configs. Before writing, content is checked by the service itself (nginx -t, haproxy -c, caddy validate, docker compose config); if the check fails, the file is automatically reverted. Every edit is saved to history.
configs.selectFileLeft: Select a file on the left.
configs.noValidation: Config validation isn't available for this service — the file was written without validation.
configs.versionHistoryHint: The first entry is created automatically before the first edit
configs.emptyHistory: No history yet — this file hasn't been edited through this interface.
configs.cloneBody: The content of {{path}} (including unsaved edits, if any) will be written under the new path — the original file is untouched.
configs.pathHint: The directory must belong to nginx, haproxy, caddy, or be a path from NKT_COMPOSE_FILES — otherwise the server rejects the write.
configs.newFileSubtitle: new file — doesn't exist on disk yet
configs.notCreated: The file wasn't created — fix the content and try again.
